The head of radiotherapy could evaluate a single 8 Gy session as the default for uncomplicated painful bone metastases (equal pain relief, more retreatment), giving Parikkala 0.0 expected nights away versus 0.0 for multi-fraction treatment [S31, S30, S60]. Within 30 days, the clinical team reviews which cases are uncomplicated [S31]. It serves the Goal 3 indicator "Patients receive treatment within target times" [S25, S24].

2. The chief physician could evaluate 5 sessions as the default for eligible patients (whole breast or chest wall without nodal radiotherapy), naming distance as a reason, as it is non-inferior to 15 [S9, S15, S14]. County-wide, this removes 0 nights away and frees 396 sessions a year (calculated, breast alone) [S33, S57, S34, S35, S60]. Within 30 days, the clinical team reviews the eligibility criteria [S15]. It serves the Goal 3 indicator "Patients receive treatment within target times" [S25, S24].

3. The quality manager could evaluate publishing schedule mix and radiotherapy use by distance band yearly [S21, S27]. Within 30 days, the director and the clinical team decide which figures to report [S26]. It serves the Goal 3 indicator "Regional differences in treatment are available and used to steer services (cross-cutting indicator)" [S26].

Distances assume the nearest unit by drive time, and the current schedule mix is unknown [S60, S16].
